- When sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >30% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent high for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 1.5x recent mean), reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >2.5x recent 18-day average, apply downward bias of 20–40% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00 over 3+ days, model often underperforms; add 5–10% upward bias to forecast for next 7 days.
